subject: Aurora Health Systems - Private deployment implementation & network ops handshake
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@aurorahealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: networking@aurorahealth.com
Date: Wed, 10 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aurora private deployment - kickoff & network prerequisites

Hi Kimberly + Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are ready to move forward with a private deployment (VPC peering + private endpoints) for a limited production rollout. Before we lock dates, our infra team asked for a short checklist and any standard diagrams you use so we can validate routing / firewall controls with our security team.

High-level asks from our side:
- CIDR requirements and overlap checks (we run 10.0.0.0/8 internally)
- Public/private endpoint behavior and egress expectations
- Minimum MTU and BGP/session expectations for peered links
- KMS / HSM integration surface for key management (we use AWS KMS with a customer-managed CMK)

Can we schedule a 60-minute network review next week? Prefer Tue/Wed mornings PT. Also looping in our internal networking alias.

Attachments: sample network diagram (we will send our diagram in a follow-up).

Thanks,
Sam Patel
Director, Platform Ops
Aurora Health Systems

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Sam —

Great to hear you're moving forward. I'll own the CS/implementation coordination and schedule the network deep-dive.

Proposed next steps (short):
1) Quick sync (60m) to walk through your network diagram and CIDR overlaps: Tue 2027-03-16 09:00 PT or Wed 2027-03-17 09:00 PT — which works?
2) We'll share our standard private/on-prem package doc and a VPC peering matrix (attached).
3) Post-sync: we open a JIRA (CS-3071) with action items and assign owners for firewall rules, KMS proof-of-fidelity, and routing tests.

For the sync I'll bring Priyom (implementation engineer) and Michael (networking runtime lead) — Priyom will outline the private endpoint behavior and Michael will cover connection performance and MTU recommendations.

I've attached the Redwood private/on-prem overview and our template VPC peering matrix so your network team can pre-fill details. Please send your network diagram before the meeting so we can pre-check for CIDR overlaps.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Implementation Lead, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@aurorahealth.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora private deployment - kickoff & network prerequisites

Sam / Kimberly —

Thanks — a few technical notes to get your network team started (I'll go into more detail on the call):

1) CIDR & routing
- Redwood recommends a non-overlapping /16 range for the peered subnet (we commonly accept /20–/16 depending on scale). If you run 10.0.0.0/8, please provide the specific subnets you can reserve for the peering (e.g., 10.240.0.0/16).
- We support both static routes and BGP sessions for dynamic routing. For high availability, BGP with route refresh is preferred.

2) MTU and fragmentation
- Minimum recommended MTU 1500. If you have jumbo frames, we can support up to 9001 but need to validate end-to-end.

3) Private endpoints & egress
- Private endpoints terminate inside the peered VPC and all control-plane traffic to Redwood is kept over the private link. Application egress (model downloads / telemetry) can be pinned to your NAT egress or routed via our managed egress depending on the plan — we'll confirm on call.

4) KMS / HSM
- We integrate with customer-managed CMKs. For HSM-backed keys, we require a key policy that allows the Redwood service principal (we'll provide exact ARNs) to perform encrypt/decrypt for serving session keys.

5) Firewall & NACLs
- We'll provide IP ranges for the private link point-to-point interfaces and a short-lived test range for connectivity validation during the smoke test.

I've attached a short checklist and a sample iptables/stateful filtering guide for the smoke test. Please drop your network diagram (aurora_network_diagram_v1.png) here before EOD Monday so we can pre-run a conflict scan.

Cheers,
Priyom Das
Senior Implementation Engineer
Redwood Inference
Attachments: networking_smoke_checklist.md, redwood_private_onprem_pack.pdf

From: Irene Lawson <irene.lawson@aurorahealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sam Patel <sam.patel@aurorahealth.com>, networking@aurorahealth.com
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 10:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora private deployment - kickoff & network prerequisites

Thanks Priyom — attaching our current network diagram and a short inventory of our peering expectations. A couple of clarifications before the call:

- HSM: we use AWS CloudHSM clusters; can Redwood key policy allow the CMK to be backed by CloudHSM? We can provide role ARNs.
- Traffic shaping: we plan to limit model downloads to off-peak windows. Is there a graceful throttling mechanism on Redwood's side for model pull or initial weights sync?
- Do you require a dedicated VLAN on our on-prem appliance, or can it sit on an existing management VLAN?

We prefer Tue 03/16 09:00 PT for the review. Attached: aurora_network_diagram_v1.png, peering_inventory.csv

Regards,
Irene Lawson
Senior Network Engineer
Aurora Health Systems
Attachments: aurora_network_diagram_v1.png, peering_inventory.csv

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Lawson <irene.lawson@aurorahealth.com>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@aurorahealth.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2027 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Aurora private deployment - kickoff & network prerequisites

Nice thread — quick operational commitments from Redwood ahead of Tue's call: 

1) Action owner assignments (we opened JIRA CS-3071):
- Priyom: pre-check CIDR overlaps and provide a recommended peering CIDR (due Mon EOD).
- Michael: prepare MTU and perf guidance plus a short test plan (due Mon EOD).
- Kimberly: coordinate scheduling, invite details, and post-call rollout milestones (will publish runbook link).

2) HSM & KMS: Yes, we support CMKs backed by CloudHSM. We'll provide the exact service principal and sample KeyPolicy statements in the runbook before the meeting.

3) Throttling & model pulls: We have an optional staged-download flow for model weights and an ingest throttle configurable per-route. For your off-peak window, we'll coordinate a staged rollout and provide telemetry hooks so you can monitor bandwidth.

4) On-prem appliance VLAN: we recommend a dedicated management VLAN for clarity in firewall rules, but we can support colocating with an existing management VLAN if you cannot provision one immediately. We'll call this out in the runbook.

5) Links & artifacts:
- JIRA: CS-3071
- Runbook (draft): https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcDefGhiJkL23M
- DocuSign preliminary agreement: https://docusign.net/aurora_private_deploy_2027

Looking forward to Tue 2027-03-16 09:00 PT. Kimberly — please send the calendar invite with a short agenda (network review, KMS/HSM, smoke test plan, timeline).

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Customer Success Ops
Redwood Inference
